::: {.entry-meta}
[measurement]{.chip .measured} Entry 61 · milestone M4
:::

The bounded diagnostic crossing the width-search basis with the final-solve basis
ran once and completed. All 108 solver calls are retained, and the saved outputs
pass an independent audit ([2139 integrity checks pass on the complete 54-pair basis grid and all 36 consumed-control comparisons reproduce the preceding study; electron flux changes sign at every state, steps reach 4.28 gB along the final basis and 4.11 gB along the search basis, and at the largest final basis the flux is a residual of order 1e-3 gB]{.claim}[C-205](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-205){.cid .st-measured}). The three settings shared with
the previous study reproduce its fluxes exactly in both backends.

Neither setting explains the sensitivity on its own. Changing only the final
basis moves electron heat flux by up to 4.3 gB; changing only the search basis
moves it by up to 4.1 gB, and the two effects do not add. At the largest final
basis tested, the flux at every state shrinks to a residual of about 1e-3 gB,
which is where most negative values occur. A smaller final basis instead finds
fast-growing high-wavenumber roots that carry much of the flux.

The native registers confirm the expected solver path: the search depends only
on its own basis, and a final solve with no unstable mode reports the input width.
They also show the search often stopping at the top of its width range.

So the reference is still not converged, and its negative values cannot yet be
used. The next candidates are a larger final basis, a wider width search and
tracking the high-wavenumber roots, each needing its own frozen request. The
current model, guard and acceptance criteria are unchanged.
